subject: ScaleWave: SLO qualification & customer-led load test — next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tan <alex@scalewave.io>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@scalewave.io>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: ScaleWave discovery — SLO targets & next steps

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we have alignment before the customer-led rehearsal.

Key SLOs you emphasized during the call:
- Text generation (non-streaming): p95 latency <= 250ms, p99 <= 450ms, target qps ~300 requests/sec for the primary route.
- Streaming (server->client): support 150 concurrent open streams with steady-state token emission ~40–60 tokens/sec per stream and end-to-end p95 chunk latency <= 200ms.
- Concurrency for conversational use-case: sustain 600 active websocket connections with KV-cache reuse for returning sessions.

Customer-led load test goals:
- Validate model variant under sustained concurrency and streaming performance.
- Verify graceful degradation: fallback to smaller model variant when we hit capacity thresholds.
- Confirm observability (per-request token breakdown + tracing) so you can map errors to prompts.

Proposed immediate actions (mutual action plan attached):
1) You provide the test traffic profile and which routes/scripts you’ll run (k6 or Locust).
2) We provide a short-lived test account, sample k6/Locust templates, and an IP allowlist for the test window.
3) Run a small dry run (30–60 minutes) followed by the full window; we’ll have an SRE on-call channel for the run.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (MAP), discovery_notes.pdf

Suggested test window options (all PST):
- Option A: Thu Sep 2 10:00–14:00 (preferred)
- Option B: Fri Sep 3 08:00–12:00

Next step: Alex, can you confirm which window works for ScaleWave and share the traffic profile file? I’ll loop in Ben (SE) to send the test creds and allowlist details.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Tan <alex@scalewave.io>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@scalewave.io>, Josh Miller <josh+load@clientops.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2026 16:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ScaleWave discovery — SLO targets & next steps

Thanks Grace — appreciate the concise summary.

We’re aligned on the SLOs. A couple clarifications from our side:
- For streaming, the streams are long-lived (~20–30s average) and we expect bursts where ~25% of streams ramp up token rates to ~120 tokens/sec for short periods. Make sure the test exercise these spike patterns.
- For concurrency, we’ll target 600 steady active websocket connections and an additional 200 short-lived sessions that arrive in waves.

We plan to run a customer-owned k6 script (we use the websocket + http modules) and will also have a Locust run for the conversational route. Attached is the initial_traffic_profile.json that maps our user distribution and spike windows.

Please provide the allowlist IPs and a test account with the probe model variant you mentioned during the call. Our ops team will need to coordinate with your networking folks for the allowlist.

We’d like to take Option A (Sep 2 10:00–14:00).

Thanks,
Alex Tan
Head of Platform Reliability
ScaleWave

Attachment: initial_traffic_profile.json

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tan <alex@scalewave.io>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Priya Desai <priya@scalewave.io>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ScaleWave discovery — SLO targets & next steps (test creds & allowlist)

Hi Alex — thanks for sending the profile. Quick operational notes and what we’re handing over for the customer-led run.

Test account and credentials (short-lived):
- username: scalewave-test@redwood.com
- api_key: redwood-test-XXXX (valid 72 hours from generation)
- model variant for probes: redwood-gen-probe-v1 (behavior matches the production family but is isolated to the test pool)

IP allowlist (add these to your egress policy for the run):
- 34.82.11.0/24
- 34.82.12.128/25
- 3.14.200.45 (static VM egress)

Attachments included: k6_template.js (k6 websocket + http scaffolding), locust_template.py (conversational route example). We recommend you reuse your initial_traffic_profile.json to param the k6 script.

Important guidance for realistic results:
- Start with a 10-minute ramp to 30% of target concurrency, hold 15 minutes, then step to 60% and hold 15 minutes, then to 100% for the final steady-state. This catches caching/compilation warmups.
- For streaming spike test: configure a short 3–5 minute window where 25% of simulated users push token_rate to the high percentile.
- Disable automatic model-quantization fallback in the first run — we want a clean baseline. We can enable it in later runs to validate graceful degradation.

Operational contacts for the window:
- Redwood SRE (on-call): seank@redwood.com
- Redwood diagnostics channel (Slack): #sw-scalewave-test (we’ll create prior to run)

Drive link with templates and sample dashboards: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/k6-templates

Attachments: k6_template.js, locust_template.py

Regards,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tan <alex@scalewave.io>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priya Desai <priya@scalewave.io>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 11:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ScaleWave discovery — SLO targets & next steps (streaming considerations)

Alex — one extra note on streaming behavior from the runtime side. For the first pass we suggest:
- Use the k6 websocket module for the streaming harness and emit token chunks at 20–30ms intervals to approximate real client consumption; avoid batching tokens server-side in the probe variant.
- We’ll enable per-token tracing so you can see p95 chunk latencies in the dashboard; keep the tracing header in your requests (x-rw-trace: 1).
- KV-cache: start with cache enabled for returning sessions but configure a control run with cache disabled so we can measure cache hit uplift.

Proposed final test window confirmation: Thu Sep 2 10:00–14:00 PST. Redwood SRE will be online and we’ll open a diagnostics bridge 15 minutes before start.

Small operational checklist for your ops team prior to run:
- Confirm egress IPs listed by Ben are whitelisted.
- Verify test account can authenticate (we’ll validate 24 hours prior).
- Share the exact git commit of your k6 script or attach the script you’ll run.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

--
Soojin Lee
Product Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks — Alex
